newsitem.title: USA: FDA proposes to withdraw Seldane approval.
newsitem.headline: FDA proposes to withdraw Seldane approval.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration said Monday it intends to withdraw its approval of terfenadine-containing Seldane and Seldane D antihistamine due to the risk of a potentially fatal heart condition when taken with some other medication.

The agency said that with the recent approval and availability of Allegra, which contains fexofenadine, which has nearly all the benefits of terfenadine but not the risks, the agency has determined that drugs with terfenadine are no longer safe.
Terfenadine and Allegra were both developed and marketed by a Hoechst AG unit based in Kansas City.
The FDA said it will also withdraw approval of generic versions of prescription antihistamine containing terfenadine.

Introduced in 1985, terfenadine was the first prescription antihistamine to relieve the symptoms of allergic hay fever without causing drowsiness. But following approval, the FDA received reports of serious and sometimes fatal cardiac irregularity associated with terfenadine when it was taken with some other medications or by patients with liver disease.

Since the cardiac risks of terfenadine were identified, several educational compaigns have been launched by the drug's sponsor and by the FDA, and the agency has implemented labeling changes and warning statements.

The FDA said in Monday's announcement, however, that although the educational and risk-reducing efforts have decreased the instances of inappropriate prescribing of terfenadine with other drugs, "such events have not been, and almost certainly cannot be, eliminated."
Approval was not withdrawn however, because the FDA felt the benefits of the terfenadine outweighed the risks when used appropriately.
After the approval of Allegra in July 1996, the FDA has determined that terfenadine-containing products shoud be removed from the market.

The FDA notice gives the manufactuers of terfenadine-containing products 30 days to request a hearing to show why approval should not be withdrawn. In the meantime, the FDA is advising patients currently taking the products to talk to their doctor about switching to alternative medications.
